gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 identifies the same defect: local implicit-function uniqueness is incorrectly promoted to global uniqueness of the full solution set, so the infimum-defined cost is not established to equal the smooth selected-branch cost.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify the invalid inference from uniqueness inside the prescribed state-pressure neighborhood to global singleton structure of S(u), leaving the globally infimized J unanchored to the C2 branch functional.

component_coverage.gold_component: The local uniqueness theorem does not imply that the full solution set S(u) is globally a singleton, so solutions outside the neighborhood may determine the infimum-defined J and invalidate the branch-based regularity and derivative arguments.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states that uniqueness holds only locally, that other solutions may remain in S(u), and that the infimum may therefore fail to coincide with the smooth branch; its repair also supplies the needed cost-attainment/coincidence condition.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 identifies that the second-variation proof uses y_Omega in L^p while the lemma assumes only y in L^p, and supplies the missing y_Omega hypothesis as the repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify the missing desired-state L^p regularity assumption required for the adjoint maximum/regularity estimates and hence for the second-variation continuity estimate.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proof requires y_Omega in L^p with p>n, but that condition is absent from the lemma's stated hypotheses, so the second-variation estimate and dependent theorem are unsupported.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction traces the proof's dependence on y_Omega in L^p, contrasts it with the lemma's actual assumption, explains the resulting loss of adjoint bounds, and explicitly proposes adding the missing condition.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 concerns the continuous solution set S(u) and the global infimum-defined J, whereas the gold issue concerns the semidiscrete solution relation, the undefined J_h, and failure to restrict or select a discrete branch. The prediction does not diagnose that discrete objective-definition defect.

ISSUE-004 identifies that the theorem quantifies over an arbitrary semidiscrete solution while convergence is proved only for a selected sequence of local minima, so the neighborhood-dependent estimates and rate are unsupported for the stated object.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify the mismatch between arbitrary existence-selected semidiscrete solutions and the specifically constructed convergent local-minimizer branch required by the proof.

component_coverage.gold_component: The control-rate theorem improperly applies convergence and local estimates to an arbitrary semidiscrete solution, although only a selected sequence of local minima is known to converge to the reference control.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly distinguishes the existence theorem from the convergence theorem, explains why the arbitrary solution need not enter the required neighborhood, and repairs the statement by selecting the convergent local-minimizer sequence.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-005 identifies the same invalid inference from an L2 state-error bound to an O(h^2) gradient-error bound, explains why inverse estimates do not apply to the continuous interpolation remainder, and gives the direct integration-by-parts repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify the false O(h^2) W^{1,6/5} gradient estimate derived from an O(h^2) L2 error and its role in the unsupported control-rate proof.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proof's O(h^2) gradient estimate is invalid because inverse estimates apply only to discrete functions and the continuous interpolation remainder has only O(h) control; the resulting rate argument therefore fails, while an H^{-1}/integration-by-parts estimate supplies the valid repair.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states the exact invalid estimate, identifies the discrete-versus-continuous error decomposition and correct rate consequence, and gives the same derivative-transfer/integration-by-parts repair using established bounds.
